Subject: Quantifying p95/p99 Delta — post-demo checklist for LedgerPay

Hi Sarah — great to meet today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on a short PoC focused on e2e latency SLOs (p95/p99):

1) Goal: Validate end-to-end p95 and p99 for the three critical flows we demoed (auth-tokenize -> embeddings -> rerank) under your peak concurrency profile. Target acceptance criteria you'd shared on the call: p95 <= 180ms, p99 <= 450ms for single-request non-streaming paths.

2) Current provider baseline (from your deck): p95 ~ 380ms, p99 ~ 980ms average across endpoints (we noted higher variance during concurrency bursts). Please confirm if those numbers represent client-observed latency (edge->client) or just model-host latency.

3) Redwood hosted assumptions we plan to test against:
   - Regional routing to us-east where your users are concentrated
   - Default batching disabled for low-latency flows; we can enable controlled batching for throughput tests
   - Streaming enabled for the long-poll responses (only applicable to the rerank flow you mentioned)

4) Data & access we need to run an apples-to-apples comparison:
   - Sample traffic profile (qps, concurrency distribution, typical payload sizes)
   - A short list of 5 representative requests/prompts to use as baseline prompts
   - A short-lived API key for a test sandbox or proxy so we can run head-to-head tests from your region

5) Proposed acceptance tests (we'll provide scripts):
   - 1k steady-state requests at your average concurrency with histograms for p50/p95/p99
   - 5 x burst windows to observe tail behavior and cache-warm effects
   - Streaming scenario: measure time-to-first-byte and time-to-final-byte

Next steps: if you confirm the baseline numbers and can share the sample profile + sandbox key, we can run an initial 48-hour comparison and share a gap analysis + runnable scripts. We also attached a short checklist PDF in the next message with the test matrix we'll execute.

Thanks — Jordan

- Streaming: we only stream the rerank flow; the other two are single-response. For streaming we care about time-to-first-byte (TTFB) because the UI shows partial results as they arrive.

Hi Sarah — Ben from the infra team here. A few technical clarifications to make the tests deterministic and reproducible: 

1) Measurement definition (what we'll report):
   - End-to-end (client-observed): time from TCP connect initiation on your client runner to final application payload received. This will include DNS and network hops when you run the client harness from your runners.
   - Model-host latency: Redwood will also report service-side timing (ingress -> egress) so you can see where tail comes from. We always provide both so teams can separate network vs compute tails.

2) Streaming vs non-streaming:
   - For streaming (rerank), we'll report TTFB and TTFB p95/p99 separately from total stream duration. TTFB is often the thing UI teams care about.
   - For non-streaming flows we capture full response latency.

3) Concurrency & batching behavior:
   - We'll disable automatic batching for the low-latency test runs and run a controlled batch-enabled test for throughput measurements.
   - For the burst windows, we'll warm the KV/cache layer first and run 5 x 30s bursts at your specified peak concurrency to observe tail amplification.

4) Acceptance criteria and pass/fail logic (proposed):
   - Pass: client-observed p95 <= 180ms AND client-observed p99 <= 450ms over a 1k-request steady-state run with concurrency = 250.
   - Conditional pass: if p95 passes but p99 misses by <=10%, we mark as "acceptable with mitigation" and run a second focused test (increase instance count/enable low-latency profile).

5) Test artifacts we'll push to you: load scripts (k6), raw histograms (HdrHistogram CSV), a summary PDF (attached), and the simulation CSV with inputs so you can rerun locally.

Attachments in this message: redwood_latency_sim_20260512.csv (sample inputs), latency_slo_matrix_v1.pdf (proposed acceptance matrix).

If that looks good I can draft the exact k6 commands and the minimal infra checklist (runner region, key rotation window) by EOD.

Cheers — Ben
